paper_title: Opportunistic detection of type 2 diabetes using deep learning from frontal chest radiographs
prediction_task: Type 2 diabetes detection from routine chest X-rays (opportunistic screening)

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: More meaningful clinical comparison would be to USPSTF recommendation (screen persons aged 35-70 with BMI≥25). How does CXR DL model perform compared to USPSTF? Within USPSTF-eligible subset, how would this affect number of people tested/diagnosed/missed?
Results section very difficult to read without Methods. Model should be explained how it would be used in clinical practice. Statistical testing should highlight utility for decision making.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Restructured results with clinical workflow context.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Despite rebuttal, would like to see correlation of DL-score and HbA1c. Many patients have consistent HbA1c levels over time — presence/absence of association provides insights into whether glycemia or adiposity features relate to diabetes detection from CXR.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added DL-score vs HbA1c correlation analysis.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Speculation that rib attenuation relates to osteoporosis should be cautious — T2D and osteoporosis correlation is subtle. More likely that rib attenuation results from increased subcutaneous fat.

reviewer_strengths.text: The explainable-AI approach presents novel aspects convincingly suggesting plausible features of CXR images associated with diabetes detection.
